title: Moss Digs
checkpoint: Reception Autumn 2, week 3 — Learning — Phase 2: new sounds l, ll, ss
note_for_grown_ups: An early Learning book using only the first sixteen sounds (up to r), so it has no h, b, f or l yet — the sentences are short on purpose. Moss's name is fully decodable with the sounds in this book — m-o-s-s — so your child can sound it out like any other word.

pages.illustration: Moss the berry-brown hedgehog side-on with both front paws raised, showing off his claws to the reader. Proud and a bit comic.
Moss nose-down in wet brown mud, back end up, spikes flecked with earth. Rich dark browns.
Three-stage sequence across the page: mud flying, the hole deepening, Moss almost gone into it. Only his back feet visible by the third.
Moss's muddy face emerging with one large hazelnut held triumphantly in his teeth, eyes shining. Close and joyful.
Pip landing at speed beside the hole, wings braking, one wing up in greeting. Mud spraying towards him.
Pip sitting squarely in the mud with an expression of dawning regret, sand-coloured feathers turning brown. Moss delighted.
Cutaway view of a snug round den under a tree root, Moss inside patting the walls smooth, dry leaves lining the floor. Cosy cross-section.

pages.text: Pip and Moss nap in the den.
pages.illustration: Closing page: both of them asleep curled together in the den, leaves pulled over, rain falling outside the entrance. Warm inside, cold outside.
